analyst_view.overall: Brentford (8th, 14 points) host Everton (6th, 16 points, three straight wins) on Monday night, two points apart. Brentford's injury list has grown over the break: captain Nathan Collins (knee, a couple of weeks) and Aaron Hickey (hamstring, several weeks) were hurt on international duty, and neither is in the numbers' missing list; Igor Thiago starts a three-match ban (counted) and Callum Wilson is expected to lead the line. Fabio Carvalho, whom the numbers count as out, has 'every chance' of being involved, while Henry, Furo, Dasilva and Milambo are still out. David Moyes says Everton are fully fit, with Jack Grealish back in training and available after his disciplinary absence. Referee Craig Pawson (3.7 cards a game) is now named and already counted.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.3 goals, already taking about 12.5% off Brentford for Thiago's ban and about 4% for Carvalho. Two things they can't see push it up a little: Brentford lose captain Collins and Hickey from the back line, which helps Barry and an Everton side with Grealish available, and Carvalho is likely to be involved after all. I go mildly higher, to about 2.4.

corners.text: The numbers say 10 corners, already counting Brentford's low recent corner count (21 in six) and Everton's slightly higher one. Lewis-Potter dropping back to left-back for Hickey changes who supplies the width rather than how much, so I stay at 10.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.2 cards, already lowering for referee Craig Pawson, who averages 3.7 a game, and for calm past meetings. Andrews calls Everton well drilled and organised, and nothing in the build-up points to a bad-tempered game, so I stay at 3.2.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.7 shots. My earlier trim assumed Brentford had no centre-forward without Thiago, but Callum Wilson is expected to start up front, and a weaker Brentford defence without Collins and Hickey should let Everton (81 shots in six, already counted) shoot a little more, so the two balance and I stay at 27.7.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.2 shots on target, already lowering Brentford for poor recent accuracy (19 on target in six). Losing Thiago's finishing is offset by Wilson leading the line and Everton facing a reshuffled back four, so I drop my earlier trim and stay at 8.2.
